reason: The floor is the likely installation site for the shared beds, but the required construction order is not yet clear.
expectation: The inspection should identify what can be installed on the floor, possibly starting the bed structure.

alternatives.reason: The steel and liner suggest a lined bed, though I do not yet know whether the frame must be built first.

effect: The steel is now installed as raised bed frames, leaving outlets above the reserved reservoir space.
reaction: The different bed depths make the crop requirements feel concrete.
reason: The frames need a food-safe lining to contain the growing beds.
expectation: The liner should fit into the raised frames to form the bed surfaces.

alternatives.reason: The reservoir also belongs beneath the bed outlets, but lining the frames seems like a natural first step.

effect: The beds are lined, but their drains still need hose connections to the reservoir.
reaction: The open drain stubs make the next plumbing task clear.
reason: The clean hose should connect the bed drains to the reservoir.
expectation: The hose will connect the drains, possibly using the available reservoir and pump.

alternatives.reason: The reservoir may need to be installed before the hose is connected.

effect: The drain hoses are installed, and the next goal is to return water through an aerated reservoir.
reaction: The downward drain runs give the plumbing a clear purpose.
reason: The reservoir and pump belong beneath the bed drains and should complete the shared water circuit.
expectation: The reservoir and pump will connect to the beds to collect and recirculate water.

effect: The hose prepared an aerating return reservoir; the bed drains still need to connect to it.
reaction: I was wrong about connecting the pump directly, but the falling return stream explains the aeration.
reason: The prepared reservoir and drained beds now appear ready to join into the shared circuit.
expectation: The bed drains will connect to the reservoir, completing the recirculating system.

effect: The reservoir and bed drains are now connected into a shared circuit with adjustable flow for each root zone, completing the chapter goals.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate plumbing pieces form a coherent system, though the beds are still empty.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the reservoir to the beds brought the separate drainage and aeration work together; the shared pump and individual flow adjustments made the design feel purposeful.

leastWorthwhile.text: The direct reservoir-to-beds attempt was slightly confusing: it failed, then automatically prepared the reservoir with a hose instead. The feedback recovered the action, but the required order had not been clear.

surprise.text: I expected the reservoir to connect directly to the beds; instead, the hose first created an aerating return, with the falling stream mixing air into the solution.

arbitrary.text: The reservoir preparation order felt somewhat arbitrary before the compatibility feedback, although the resulting explanation gave the hose a physical purpose.

continue.text: Yes, I would choose to continue: the physically explained plumbing was interesting, and I would like to see how the empty beds become productive.
